name: list_projects
description: List the projects in this database, with their type, root paths and node counts. `root_path` is the host tree each project reads; an organization reads none of its own. `members` is what an organization holds and `organizations` is what holds this project; describe_project says what each one is for. Types are "codebase" (the default), "docs", "config" - all indexed trees, differing only as a search filter - "organization", a project that is no tree of its own but a set of them, holding other projects by reference so one search reaches all of them - and "memory" and "suggestions", which are not trees at all: the built-in _memory and _suggestions hold records written through save_memory and save_suggestion.

name: describe_project
description: Say what one project is: its type, the sentence written about it, the tree it reads, how much of it is indexed and the organizations holding it. An organization answers with the projects it holds, each described the same way, which is how a session opened on one learns what it can reach. Given a path it answers for whichever project reads that tree, which is how a session works out which project it is standing in

path.description: A host directory, typically the working directory. The project whose own directory contains it is the one described, and naming it overrides the project argument

name: drop_project
description: Remove an indexed codebase from the database. Reports what the drop costs and deletes nothing unless confirm is true

name.description: Name of the project to drop. Always named explicitly, never taken from the session, so a call cannot delete by omission

confirm.description: Perform the delete. Absent or false, the tool only reports what would be lost

name: get_code_graph_neighbors
description: Get the related nodes and dependencies of a file or code entity, and the memories, plans and suggestions written about it or a directory above it

node_id.description: File or node identifier, for example src/index.ts

name: get_project_links
description: How projects reach each other: which project uses which, by what relation (an image it runs, a role it applies, a package or a Terraform module it depends on, a host it deploys to, an OS package it installs, a bucket it uses, or a relation declared by hand), with counts and sample node pairs, walked up to depth projects away. Also what this project provides, the names it takes that no indexed project provides, and the names several projects provide, which are left unlinked rather than guessed. Built from the graph alone; no embedding is needed

direction.description: outgoing: what this project uses; incoming: what uses it; both (the default)

depth.description: How many projects away to walk (default 1, max 3)

relation.description: Keep only links of this relation, e.g. uses_image

node_id.description: Keep only the links leaving or reaching this node; walks one project away

name: trace
description: Follow one node across projects: what its directory provides (an image, a package, a role, a module, a host), which projects take it, what applies the taker there (a class included by a role, a role a node selects, a module a circuit uses), and what those use in turn, such as the host a node deploys to and the project that creates it. Answers with the steps, each saying which edge or matched name made it, and the chains they form. Built from the graph alone; no embedding is needed

node_id.description: Where to start: a directory (src/app/), a file or a symbol

max_steps.description: How many steps to take at most (default 60, max 300)

name: search_text
description: Find a string in the files themselves, the way grep does: every line of the indexed trees containing it, with the file and the line number, unranked. For an exact name - a host, a key, an error message - that search_code splits into words. The trees are read where they are mounted; no file text is kept in the database. `loose` matches a name whatever separates its words (web_01_example_com finds web-01.example.com), `regex` takes the pattern as a regular expression. Projects are read in turn until the limit is met

pattern.description: The text to find, matched without case

loose.description: Ignore what separates the words (default false)

regex.description: Read pattern as a regular expression

path.description: A glob narrowing the files, e.g. **/*.yaml

project_type.description: Search every project of this kind instead of one project. Cannot be combined with a named project. Types are "codebase" (the default), "docs", "config" - all indexed trees, differing only as a search filter - "organization", a project that is no tree of its own but a set of them, holding other projects by reference so one search reaches all of them - and "memory" and "suggestions", which are not trees at all: the built-in _memory and _suggestions hold records written through save_memory and save_suggestion.

name: find_linked_name
description: Who provides and who takes a name across projects: a host, an image, a package, a role, a bucket. Answers with every project and node that defines it (a machine resource, a VM file, a build) and every one that uses it (a node deploying to the host, an inventory, a class installing the package), so a question about a host or an artifact starts here and continues with trace from a node it names. Case and separators do not matter (alpha_web_01 finds alpha-web-01.example.com), a host is also found by its first label and an image by its last path segment. Empty on both sides means no indexed project defines or uses the name in a form the indexer reads; it may still be mentioned in text. Built from the graph alone; no embedding is needed

name.description: The name, e.g. web-01.example.com or alpha-worker

kind.description: Keep only names of this kind

project_type.description: Search every project of this kind instead of one project. Cannot be combined with a named project. Types are "codebase" (the default), "docs", "config" - all indexed trees, differing only as a search filter - "organization", a project that is no tree of its own but a set of them, holding other projects by reference so one search reaches all of them - and "memory" and "suggestions", which are not trees at all: the built-in _memory and _suggestions hold records written through save_memory and save_suggestion.

name: save_project_link
description: Declare a relation between two projects that no manifest states: a service deploys to an infrastructure repository, a docs repository documents a codebase, one calls the other's API. Saving the same relation again replaces its note

relation.description: deploys_to, documents, depends_on, calls, generated_from, implements, or any other verb

source_id.description: A node of the source project, when the relation leaves a part of it (default ./, the whole tree)

target_id.description: A node of the target project (default ./, the whole tree)

name: drop_project_link
description: Remove a relation declared with save_project_link, named by the same project, target, relation and node ids

name: save_project_export
description: Say that a project provides a name no file of it states: an image its CI builds, a package it publishes. Every project that takes that name is linked to it from then on

name.description: As other projects write it; an image tag and digest are dropped, a Python name is normalized, a host is lower case, a module source loses its getter, scheme and ref

node_id.description: The directory that is the thing (default ./, the whole tree)

name: drop_project_export
description: Remove an export saved with save_project_export. One the index run found in a manifest stays, and is said so

name: search_code_nodes
description: Find nodes by name or identifier, in one project or across every project of a kind. Naming an organization searches every project it holds, which is what an organization is for

project_type.description: Search every project of this kind instead of one project. Cannot be combined with a named project. Types are "codebase" (the default), "docs", "config" - all indexed trees, differing only as a search filter - "organization", a project that is no tree of its own but a set of them, holding other projects by reference so one search reaches all of them - and "memory" and "suggestions", which are not trees at all: the built-in _memory and _suggestions hold records written through save_memory and save_suggestion.

query.description: Substring matched against the node name and id

limit.description: Maximum rows to return (default 20, max 50). A search spanning projects splits it between them rather than spending it all on the first

name: search_code
description: Search by meaning as well as by name: a question in plain words ("where is the retry logic") is answered from the text of the indexed files, ranked together with the identifier matches search_code_nodes makes. Answers with the file and the line range to read. Results are reranked by exact identifier, path, node type and graph links. Reach for search_code_nodes instead when the exact name of a symbol is already known

project_type.description: Search every project of this kind instead of one project. Cannot be combined with a named project. Types are "codebase" (the default), "docs", "config" - all indexed trees, differing only as a search filter - "organization", a project that is no tree of its own but a set of them, holding other projects by reference so one search reaches all of them - and "memory" and "suggestions", which are not trees at all: the built-in _memory and _suggestions hold records written through save_memory and save_suggestion.

query.description: What to look for, as words rather than as a pattern. The identifiers in it are matched literally as well

rerank.description: Rerank the fused candidates (default true). false returns the plain reciprocal rank fusion order, for comparison

mode.description: Which half answers, to trace a bad answer to the half that produced it (default "hybrid", both fused). "lexical" matches words and names only and embeds nothing; "vector" matches by meaning only, and is refused with the reason when the query cannot be embedded or nothing in scope has embeddings. The answer opens with a line naming the mode

name: get_context
description: Assemble the engineering context for a question in one call: the hybrid search and the reranker pick the seeds, the graph is expanded around them into what depends on them, the tests near them, what they define, call and import, the result is deduplicated and cut to a token budget. Every entry says why it is there and whether it was found by the search or reached through the graph, and `knowledge` carries what memories, plans and suggestions say about the hits. Reach for this first on a broad question ("how does X work"); search_code and the graph tools stay for precise navigation. Source text is read from the mounted trees for the chunks a project has, so a project without embeddings answers with references and summaries alone

project_type.description: Assemble from every project of this kind instead of one project. Cannot be combined with a named project. Types are "codebase" (the default), "docs", "config" - all indexed trees, differing only as a search filter - "organization", a project that is no tree of its own but a set of them, holding other projects by reference so one search reaches all of them - and "memory" and "suggestions", which are not trees at all: the built-in _memory and _suggestions hold records written through save_memory and save_suggestion.

query.description: The question, in words. The identifiers in it are matched literally as well

token_budget.description: How large the packet may be, estimated at four characters per token (default 12000, min 200, max 60000). The budget is spent on the search hits first, then on what depends on them, the tests, what they define, what they call and what they import, in that order

seeds.description: How many search hits the expansion starts from (default 8, max 25)

expand.description: Hops to follow per relationship tier, 0 to switch one off (max 2). Defaults to one hop of each

include_chunks.description: Carry the source text of the matched chunks (default true). false returns references, summaries and relations only, which is far cheaper

rerank.description: Rerank the seeds before expanding (default true). false seeds from the plain fusion order, for comparison

detail.description: What the packet spends its budget on (default "auto"). "summary" climbs from each hit to the repository root and lists what the hits hold, with source for the best two only; "source" is code first. "auto" picks source when the question names code (an identifier, a path, a call) and the summary ladder for a question in words or a small budget

name: shortest_path
description: Find the shortest chain of relations between two nodes of the graph

source_id.description: Node the path starts from, for example src/index.ts

name: find_definition
description: Where a symbol is defined: the node, its file and line, the class holding it and its summary. Every node of that name when it is ambiguous

symbol.description: The symbol: "Class.method", "function", "Class", or with the extractor's own "name()"

file_path.description: File the symbol is defined in, when several nodes share its name

name: find_callers
description: Who calls a symbol. Graph calls edges (resolved within one file by the extractor) and, across files, call sites matched by name in the indexed text; every entry says which evidence put it there

symbol.description: The symbol: "Class.method", "function", "Class", or with the extractor's own "name()"

file_path.description: File the symbol is defined in, when several nodes share its name

max_hops.description: How far to follow the graph (default 1, max 3)

name: find_callees
description: What a symbol calls, or for a class what its methods call. Graph edges only, so a call into another file is not listed

symbol.description: The symbol: "Class.method", "function", "Class", or with the extractor's own "name()"

file_path.description: File the symbol is defined in, when several nodes share its name

max_hops.description: How far to follow the graph (default 1, max 3)

name: find_references
description: Everything that refers to a symbol: incoming graph edges of any kind but containment, and every mention of its name in the indexed text

symbol.description: The symbol: "Class.method", "function", "Class", or with the extractor's own "name()"

file_path.description: File the symbol is defined in, when several nodes share its name

max_hops.description: How far to follow the graph (default 1, max 3)

name: find_implementations
description: What extends or implements a class or interface: inherits edges and `extends X` / `implements X` / `class Y(X)` in the indexed text

symbol.description: The symbol: "Class.method", "function", "Class", or with the extractor's own "name()"

file_path.description: File the symbol is defined in, when several nodes share its name

max_hops.description: How far to follow the graph (default 1, max 3)

name: find_tests
description: The tests that reach a symbol: references and callers up to two hops away that live in a test file

symbol.description: The symbol: "Class.method", "function", "Class", or with the extractor's own "name()"

file_path.description: File the symbol is defined in, when several nodes share its name

max_hops.description: How far to follow the graph (default 1, max 3)

name: impact_analysis
description: What a change to a symbol or a file could reach: what depends on it directly and indirectly, the tests, the public API (routes, controllers, handlers, servers) and the configuration among them, with counts and the files. Every entry says whether a graph edge or a text match (NAME_MATCH) put it there. `knowledge` lists the memories, plans and suggestions about what the change reaches

symbol.description: A symbol as for find_definition, or a file path such as src/auth/jwt.ts

file_path.description: File the symbol is defined in, when several nodes share its name

depth.description: How many hops of dependents to follow (default 3, max 3)

name: save_node_summary
description: Save or update a summary for a specific node in the code graph

node_id.description: The unique identifier of the node (e.g. file path)

summary.description: The summary content for the node

name: get_node_summary
description: Retrieve the summary, file path, and type for a specific node

node_id.description: The unique identifier of the node (e.g. file path)

name: get_overview
description: Read the summary tree under a directory or file: the repository is "./", a directory id ends in a slash ("src/api/"). Each item carries its summary, who wrote it (auto, llm, manual) and how many children it has, so a broad question starts here and drills down one directory at a time before any source is read

path.description: Directory or file node to start from (default "./", the repository root)

depth.description: Levels below the start to list (default 2, max 6)

include_entities.description: List the symbols inside files as well (default false)

token_budget.description: How large the tree may be, at four characters per token (default 4000, min 200, max 60000)

name: save_plan
description: Create or update a persistent execution plan. Plans are stored across projects and outlive the codebase they were written for

plan_id.description: Identifier of the plan, unique across the whole database. Saving under an existing one overwrites that plan

status.description: Status of the plan (e.g., active, completed, archived)

type.description: What the record is, apart from its lifecycle: "plan" (the default) for work executed once, "template" for a form to copy, "procedure" for a routine run on demand. Free text, like status.

nodes.description: The code this is about: node ids (src/auth/, src/auth/jwt.ts, a symbol id) in the project it is about, or { project, node_id } for another one. Each must exist. Given, it replaces the nodes stored before; left out, they are kept. A directory covers what is below it

name: get_plans
description: Retrieve execution plans filtered by project and status. Global plans, the ones saved without a project, are always included. Each plan lists its `prompts` by id and status: an active plan with none is not executed until its prompt is written. `roadmap_items` names the roadmap items the plan carries out

type.description: Filter plans by type (default 'plan'), "*" for every type. What the record is, apart from its lifecycle: "plan" (the default) for work executed once, "template" for a form to copy, "procedure" for a routine run on demand. Free text, like status.

node_id.description: Keep only the records about this node or a directory above it, so a file finds what was written about its module

node_project.description: The project node_id is in, when it is not the one this read is about

name: drop_plan
description: Delete a plan outright, for one written by mistake or moved elsewhere; its prompts go with it, and a roadmap item it carried is left with no plan. Finished work is retired by re-saving it as completed

plan_id.description: Identifier of the plan to delete. It is unique across the database, so no project is named

name: save_prompt
description: Create or update the execution prompt of a plan: what a session is handed to carry the plan out, with its file set, constraints and what done means. Written right after the plan is approved and saved; a plan with no prompt is not executed. The prompt is about whatever its plan is about, so no project is named

prompt_id.description: Identifier of the prompt, unique across the whole database. Saving under an existing one overwrites that prompt

plan_id.description: The plan this prompt executes. It must exist: save the plan first

title.description: One line naming what the prompt has done

content.description: The prompt itself, complete enough to be executed without the conversation it came from

status.description: Status of the prompt (e.g., active, completed). Free text, like a plan's status; retire a prompt together with its plan

name: get_prompts
description: Retrieve execution prompts, by project and status or for one plan. Prompts of global plans are always included

status.description: Filter prompts by status (default 'active'), "*" for every status

plan_id.description: Keep only the prompts of this plan, whatever project it is about

name: drop_prompt
description: Delete a prompt outright, for one written by mistake. Its plan stays. A prompt that was carried out is retired by re-saving it as completed

prompt_id.description: Identifier of the prompt to delete. It is unique across the database, so no project is named

name: save_roadmap
description: Create or update a roadmap: an ordered list of what is to be done for a project, each item tied to the plan that carries it out. This writes the roadmap itself; its items are written one by one with save_roadmap_item. Work agreed for later goes onto a roadmap rather than into a plan's free text

roadmap_id.description: Identifier of the roadmap, unique across the whole database. Saving under an existing one overwrites its title, introduction, status and project, and leaves its items alone

content.description: An introduction: what the roadmap is for and what constrains everything on it. Optional

status.description: Status of the roadmap (e.g., active, completed, archived)

name: get_roadmaps
description: Retrieve roadmaps with their items in order. Each item carries its state, the plan that carries it out with that plan's status, and that plan's prompts, so the walk from an item to its plan and on to its prompt costs no further call. Global roadmaps are always included

status.description: Filter roadmaps by status (default 'active'), "*" for every status

roadmap_id.description: Read this one roadmap, whatever its project and status

name: drop_roadmap
description: Delete a roadmap and every item on it, for one written by mistake. The plans its items named stay

roadmap_id.description: Identifier of the roadmap to delete. It is unique across the database, so no project is named

name: save_roadmap_item
description: Create or change one item of a roadmap. On an existing item only the arguments given change, so marking one done is this call with a status alone. A plan for work that is on a roadmap is named on its item, and the item is marked when the plan is completed: nothing does that silently

roadmap_id.description: The roadmap the item is on. It must exist

item_id.description: Short slug naming the item, unique within its roadmap

title.description: One line naming the item. Required for a new item

content.description: What the item means and what done looks like. Optional

section.description: The heading the item is listed under, free text (e.g. Stability, Parsers). An empty string is no section

status.description: Where the item stands, free text: open (the default), next, in progress, done, dropped

plan_id.description: The plan that carries the item out. It must exist. An empty string unties the item from its plan

position.description: The place in the roadmap's order, counted from 1. A new item goes last when it is left out; what stood at that place or after it moves down one

name: drop_roadmap_item
description: Delete one item of a roadmap, for one written by mistake. An item that is no longer wanted is kept with the status dropped

roadmap_id.description: The roadmap the item is on

name: save_memory
description: Write down something worth keeping across sessions: a convention, a decision, a fact about how a repository works. Stored in the built-in _memory project, not derived from any tree, so nothing re-indexes it away

memory_id.description: Short slug naming the topic, for example "commit-style". Unique within one `about` scope; saving under an existing one overwrites that memory

title.description: One line naming what this is

summary.description: One-line gist, which is what listings and searches show. Taken from the title when absent

tags.description: Free-text labels a later read can filter on

nodes.description: The code this is about: node ids (src/auth/, src/auth/jwt.ts, a symbol id) in the project it is about, or { project, node_id } for another one. Each must exist. Given, it replaces the nodes stored before; left out, they are kept. A directory covers what is below it

name: get_memory
description: Read stored memories in full. Without a memory_id it lists the scope, and memories about no project in particular are always included

memory_id.description: Read one memory. Either the slug, which is looked up in the named scope and then globally, or a full "<about>/<slug>" id

tags.description: Keep only memories carrying all of these tags

node_id.description: Keep only the records about this node or a directory above it, so a file finds what was written about its module

node_project.description: The project node_id is in, when it is not the one this read is about

query.description: Substring matched against the title, the gist and the text

name: drop_memory
description: Delete a memory that turned out to be wrong or is no longer true

memory_id.description: Full "<about>/<slug>" id, as get_memory reports it. A bare slug is resolved against `about`

name: save_suggestion
description: Record a gap: something the graph or the context did not have, and the concrete change that would fix it. Saving under an id that already exists is how a gap is reported again - it keeps the first sighting, moves the last, counts the hit, and reopens a suggestion that had been resolved. Stored in the built-in _suggestions project

suggestion_id.description: Short slug naming the gap, for example "hcl-no-parser". Derive it from the gap itself and keep it stable: that is what makes the second report count rather than duplicate. Unique within one `about` scope

title.description: One line naming what was missing

detail.description: What was missing, what had to be done by hand instead, and the concrete change that would remove the need

summary.description: One-line gist, which is what listings show. Taken from the title when absent

kind.description: What kind of gap this is: "empty-lookup" (a query that found nothing that exists), "missing-summary", "thin-summary" (one that reads like a summary and answers nothing), "not-indexed", "no-parser", "stale-index", "missing-tool". Free text

lever.description: Which lever closing this gap moves: "tokens" (the answer was re-derived by hand), "coverage" (the graph does not describe it at all) or "runtime" (it was answerable, but slowly). Free text

status.description: Where this stands: "open" (the default), "resolved" once the change landed, "wontfix" when it will not. Free text, like a plan's status

bump.description: Whether this call is a fresh sighting (default true). Pass false to correct the wording or set the status without counting a hit

query.description: The question or search the graph failed to answer. Kept with the gap, up to twenty distinct ones, so a fix can be checked against what was actually asked

nodes.description: The code this is about: node ids (src/auth/, src/auth/jwt.ts, a symbol id) in the project it is about, or { project, node_id } for another one. Each must exist. Given, it replaces the nodes stored before; left out, they are kept. A directory covers what is below it

name: get_suggestions
description: Read recorded gaps, the most often hit first. Defaults to the open ones, and gaps about no project in particular are always included

suggestion_id.description: Read one suggestion. Either the slug, which is looked up in the named scope and then globally, or a full "<about>/<slug>" id

status.description: Where this stands: "open" (the default), "resolved" once the change landed, "wontfix" when it will not. Free text, like a plan's status. Defaults to "open"; "*" reads every status

kind.description: Keep only gaps of this kind

node_id.description: Keep only the records about this node or a directory above it, so a file finds what was written about its module

node_project.description: The project node_id is in, when it is not the one this read is about

group_by.description: Roll the gaps up instead of listing them: by kind, lever or about, or by the directory of the nodes they name - each group with how many records, their hits summed, and the most hit ones

query.description: Substring matched against the title, the gist and the detail

name: drop_suggestion
description: Delete a suggestion written by mistake. A gap that has since been closed is retired instead, with save_suggestion status: "resolved" and bump: false, so the count it accumulated is not lost

suggestion_id.description: Full "<about>/<slug>" id, as get_suggestions reports it. A bare slug is resolved against `about`

name: get_file_hash
description: Get the stored parse hash of a file, taken from its content and the parser revision

name: clear_file_hash
description: Clear the stored hash for a file, forcing a re-index

name: set_file_hash
description: Manually set the stored parse hash of a file

name: list_indexed_files
description: List all files currently tracked in the indexed_files table

name: list_skills
description: List the skills a session on the project should have installed, each with its version: the sha256 its local copy must carry in the `version:` field of its frontmatter

name: get_skill
description: Return one skill's current text, version stamped, and the path to write it to. Written unchanged, it replaces an outdated copy
